culture: Piazza Archimede in Ortigia (Syracuse) features the Fountain of Diana, with Diana, nymphs and tritons
The fountain is considered the heart of Ortigia
Ortigia's Cathedral (Duomo) stands right next to the square
The Duomo is built into an ancient Greek temple, with the columns embedded in its walls
The temple was dedicated to Athena and is over 2,000 years old
The ancient golden columns can still be seen inside the Cathedral
Ortigia is an island where the sea is always close
In November Ortigia has fewer people, gentle sun and little wind
Via Maestranza leads from the piazza to the seafront (lungomare)
Locals take a daily short walk (due passi) to the sea and sit on a bench in the piazza
Archimedes is the famous ancient scholar of Syracuse, and his story is tied to the piazza
Italian phrases: Buongiorno (good morning), A domani (see you tomorrow), Buona passeggiata (enjoy your walk), mi fa piacere (I'm glad), Le piace...? (formal: do you like...?)
